[00:49] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [pause] That's a fair read of our website.
[00:53] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): You're agreeing?
[00:55] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Our marketing is aimed at companies with a governance function. You don't have one, so it isn't aimed at you.
[01:04] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): So why are you calling?

[02:01] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): How much of the four months is waiting?
[02:04] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] I don't know. That's part of why we're doing this.

[02:14] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Well. Genuinely well. Their team's been good.

[02:47] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'm being realistic about it. Unless there's something in your evaluation that isn't going well, in which case I'd want to know what.
[02:57] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] There is one thing.
[03:00] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Go on.

[03:23] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Nobody ever does.
[03:25] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): It'll be six.
[03:27] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd want to be honest — there's a good chance we don't have a connector either. What's the system?
[03:34] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): I'd rather not say on a cold call, if that's alright.

[04:19] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Doing what?
[04:21] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Conceding things.
[04:23] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd rather concede the things that are true and be believed on the things that aren't.
[04:29] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] Alright. What's the argument you would make?

[04:52] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): It waits.
[04:54] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): For how long?
[04:56] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] Depends. Weeks.
[04:59] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then the question for your evaluation — for either vendor — is whether the people who own the process can change the process without him. That's testable in a week and most evaluations don't test it.
[05:15] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): How would you test it?
[05:17] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Have someone in operations, not your developer, build one real workflow. Not with the developer sitting next to them. And see what happens.
[05:29] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] That's a good test.
[05:33] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's the test that predicts whether you're happy in two years. Run it against Tray — I mean that, run it against Tray, you're three weeks in and it costs you nothing.
[05:46] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): And if they pass?
[05:48] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then buy Tray. You'll have made a good decision for a good reason.
[05:54] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [laughs] You are the strangest salesperson I've spoken to this year.
[05:59] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'll take that.
[06:01] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Look — I'm not going to restart the evaluation. We've got a decision date and I'm not moving it.
[06:09] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I wouldn't ask you to.
[06:11] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): But I'll do this. Send me something short — not a deck — on how you'd approach the seven-stage thing, and specifically on the operations-can-change-it question. If we go with Tray and it doesn't work out, I'll know who to call.

[07:37] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): A month of delay on a cell? Roughly, we recognise revenue on commissioning, so — a month is a month of revenue on a two hundred thousand pound order.

[07:53] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Eleven at the moment.

answer.summary: Across these calls, the capabilities prospects seem to care about most are: workflow orchestration across systems, reliable integrations, and visibility/governance. The most repeated specifics are narrowing the first phase to one real workflow, validating required operations on connectors and APIs, keeping run history/auditability, and handling exceptions with branching, retries, queues, and stateful execution. Security controls and AI constraints also come up a lot, but usually as gating requirements rather than the core product promise.
